revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Professional Basketball Salaries
revealWordProblem.text: Two box plots show the salaries of 15 players on two professional teams. Team A: least $1M, Q1 $2M, median $4M, Q3 $9M, greatest $15M. Team B: least $2M, Q1 $3.5M, median $4M, Q3 $6M, greatest $9M. A player hopes to be drafted. Find the range and the IQR for each team, then decide which team he should hope for and explain your reasoning.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Team A: range = 15 − 1 = $14M, IQR = 9 − 2 = $7M. Team B: range = 9 − 2 = $7M, IQR = 6 − 3.5 = $2.5M. Both teams have the same median salary, $4M, so the median cannot separate them. Team A has far more variability: a few players earn very large salaries while the bottom quarter earns under $2M. Team B's salaries are much less spread out, so a typical player is more likely to earn close to $4M. If the player wants the best chance at a salary near the middle, he should hope for Team B; if he is betting on becoming a star and is willing to risk the low end, Team A pays the highest salaries.

conceptIntro.heading: Let's build it together — How spread out is the data?
conceptIntro.intro: A measure of center like the median tells you where the data sits. It does not tell you how far apart the values are. Two classes can share the same median and still look nothing alike. Range and interquartile range are the two numbers that describe that spread. We'll walk through a worked example, try one together, then you'll try a few with hints right there when you need them.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Range = greatest − least, and it covers every value. Interquartile range = Q3 − Q1, and it covers only the middle half, so one faraway value cannot stretch it.

iDo.title: Watch me measure the spread of the test scores
lines: Here are 20 history test scores in order: 68, 70, 73, 74, 75, 76, 77, 80, 82, 83, 84, 85, 86, 86, 88, 88, 90, 90, 93, 94. Ordering them first is what makes every step after this possible.
Range: I subtract the least value from the greatest. 94 − 68 = 26. The scores span 26 points from end to end.
Now the quartiles. The median splits the 20 scores into two halves of 10. The median is halfway between the 10th and 11th values: (83 + 84) ÷ 2 = 83.5.
Q1 is the median of the lower 10 values: halfway between 75 and 76, so Q1 = 75.5. Q3 is the median of the upper 10: halfway between 88 and 88, so Q3 = 88.
Interquartile range: IQR = Q3 − Q1 = 88 − 75.5 = 12.5. The middle half of the students' scores differed by only 12.5 points, even though the full range was 26.

weDo.title: Let's do one together
lines: Class A's box plot reads: least 62, Q1 74, median 81, Q3 87, greatest 90. Find the range first.
Range = 90 − 62 = 28 points from the lowest score to the highest.
Now the IQR: subtract Q1 from Q3. IQR = 87 − 74 = 13 points across the middle half.
Say what each one means: the whole class's scores span 28 points, but the middle half of the class is packed into 13 points.
Sentence frame — say it with me: "The multiples/steps I need are ___ , and the answer is ___ ."

onLevel.stem: Two students both scored 80 on a make-up test — one joins Class A (range 28, IQR 13) and one joins Class B (range 20, IQR 8). Both classes have a median of 81. Predict how each class's IQR changes, and explain your reasoning.
onLevel.sampleAnswer: Each new score of 80 lands just below the median of 81, which is inside the box for both classes. Adding a value inside the middle of the data pulls the quartiles slightly toward the center, so each IQR either stays the same or shrinks a little; neither can grow much, because nothing was added out at the extremes. The ranges do not change at all, since 80 is neither a new least nor a new greatest value for either class. The comparison holds: Class B's scores stay the more tightly clustered of the two.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake with Range and Interquartile Range is adding the two quartiles instead of subtracting them — writing IQR = Q3 + Q1. With Q1 = 42 and Q3 = 58 that gives 100, which is larger than the data set's entire range of 20. Every measure of variation is a DIFFERENCE, and the IQR can never exceed the range, because the middle half is part of the whole span. If your IQR comes out bigger than your range, you added when you should have subtracted.

connect.promptQuestion: Which class scored better overall, and how do the range and the IQR show it?
connect.prompt: Class A's range is ___ and Class B's range is ___, so Class A's scores are more ___. Class A's IQR is ___ and Class B's IQR is ___, so the middle half of Class B is packed into a ___ stretch of points. Because 75% of Class B scored ___ or more, Class B did better ___.

check.stem: What is the range of Class A's scores?
What is the interquartile range of Class B's scores?
check.explanation: IQR = Q3 − Q1 = 84 − 76 = 8 points — the width of Class B's box.

check.stem: Both classes have a median of 81. What do the smaller range and smaller IQR tell you about Class B?
choices: Class B's scores are less spread out, so more students scored near the median
Class B's best score was higher
Class B's median is actually larger
check.explanation: A smaller range and a smaller IQR both mean less variability: Class B's scores cluster more tightly around the same median of 81.

connect.modelAnswer: Class A's range is 28 and Class B's range is 20, so Class A's scores are more spread out. Class A's IQR is 13 and Class B's IQR is 8, so the middle half of Class B is packed into a smaller stretch of points. Because 75% of Class B scored 76 or more, Class B did better overall.

exitTicket.stem: Quick check — you've got this: A box plot has Q1 = 20 and Q3 = 36, with a least value of 10 and a greatest value of 50. What is the IQR, and what does it tell you?
choices: IQR = 16; the middle half of the data spans 16 units
IQR = 40; the data spans 40 units from end to end
IQR = 28; 28 is halfway between the quartiles
exitTicket.explanation: IQR = Q3 − Q1 = 36 − 20 = 16. Because it runs from Q1 to Q3, it describes only the middle half of the values — the width of the box.
choiceFeedback: 50 − 10 = 40 is the RANGE, which uses the extremes. The IQR uses only the quartiles.
The IQR is a difference, not a sum. Subtract Q1 from Q3.
28 is the midpoint between 20 and 36 — that is a center, not a width.
hints: The IQR is the width of the box on a box plot.
The box runs from Q1 to Q3, so subtract: 36 − 20.
Then say what that number covers: all of the data, or just the middle half?

questions.stem: In a histogram, what does the height of each bar represent?
choices: The average of the data in that interval
The frequency (count) of data in that interval
questions.explanation: Each bar's height shows the frequency — how many data values fall within that interval.

questions.stem: A histogram bar for the interval 20–29 reaches a height of 7. What does the 7 tell you?
questions.explanation: A bar's height is the frequency — here, 7 values land in the 20–29 interval.

questions.stem: A histogram has intervals: 0–4, 5–9, 10–14, 15–19. What is the width of each interval?
questions.explanation: Each interval covers 5 values (0,1,2,3,4 then 5,6,7,8,9 etc.), so the width is 5.
